assessment.actual_result: The resume tailoring experience was fast and intuitive, and the platform successfully identified ATS issues, skill gaps, and improvement opportunities. However, when the score changed after making edits, it was difficult to understand which specific changes influenced the result or how I could better demonstrate skills that I already possess but may not have described effectively. Additionally, customization options were limited, making it difficult to create custom sections or organize information such as "Why I Am a Strong Fit for This Role" and "Language Proficiency" and "Leadership Experience" in alternative layouts.
assessment.attempted_action: I was editing the tailored version of my resume generated by Myro to improve my Myro Score and better align my profile with the target roles. I wanted to strengthen the resume by incorporating relevant skills, refining content based on Myro's recommendations, and presenting my experience in the most effective way while maintaining ATS compatibility.
assessment.biggest_problem: The Myro Score is a central part of the experience, but it is not always clear what specific changes influence the score. While I understood that the score is based on evidence of skills within the resume rather than simply listing skills, there was limited guidance on how users can better demonstrate skills they already possess but may not have articulated effectively.
assessment.expected_result: I expected Myro to clearly show how my edits affected the score and which changes strengthened or weakened the evidence for specific skills. I also expected the resume editor to provide enough flexibility to customize the resume structure through custom sections and layout options so that I could better highlight role-specific strengths, leadership experience, language proficiency, or other relevant information.
assessment.most_useful_moment: The most useful moment was uploading my CV and receiving a tailored version within seconds. What stood out was that Myro did not stop at identifying ATS issues and skill gaps; it provided actionable next steps through targeted skill assessments and recommendations, making it easy to understand not only what needed improvement but also how to improve it. This made the experience feel outcome-oriented rather than just informational.
assessment.preserve: The resume upload, CV analysis, ATS validation, and resume tailoring workflow should remain unchanged. The experience is fast, intuitive, and action-oriented. What stood out most was that Myro did not stop at identifying gaps; it provided practical next steps through skill assessments and recommendations, making it easy for users to take action on the feedback immediately.
assessment.priority_improvement:
Introduce greater transparency around the Myro Score through a "Skill Evidence Assistant" and score-change breakdown.

The feature should show:

Which skills currently have strong evidence in the resume.
Which skills have weak or missing evidence.
Why the score changed after each edit.
Suggestions for stronger achievement-based phrasing that better demonstrates a skill.
assessment.priority_reason:
The Myro Score appears to be one of the platform's core value propositions and influences how users evaluate their progress. Users are more likely to trust and act on recommendations when they understand the reasoning behind them. Improving score transparency would reduce trial-and-error editing, help users make more meaningful improvements, and reinforce confidence in Myro's recommendations.

Additionally, if users can clearly see which skills lack evidence and receive guidance on how to strengthen them, they can make those improvements directly within Myro rather than switching to external tools or seeking additional feedback elsewhere. This creates a more complete end-to-end experience where users can identify gaps, understand them, act on them, and measure the impact of their changes in a single platform. While editor customization is valuable, score transparency would benefit nearly every user interacting with the product and therefore has the highest potential impact.

assessment.attempted_action: I was trying to check and test the Myro CV feature.I can upload my resume, improve it using the AI suggestions, explore jobs that match my profile, save interesting opportunities, and keep track of our applications. It's a simple way to manage the entire job search process from one place instead of switching between multiple websites.
assessment.biggest_problem: The biggest issue I noticed was with the job matches and tracker. Some of the recommended jobs didn't seem very relevant to my profile, and while the tracker helped me stay organized, I felt it could offer more features like reminders, notes, or clearer progress updates to make managing applications easier.
assessment.expected_result: I expect a smoother and more organized job search experience. The platform helps you improve your resume with AI feedback, suggests jobs that match your profile, and lets you track all your applications in one place. It also gives you a better idea of how well your CV aligns with the roles you're applying for, making it easier to prepare and apply with confidence.
assessment.most_useful_moment: What I found most useful was the CV review. It gave me quick feedback on my resume and highlighted a few things I could improve. I also liked how the job recommendations matched my profile, so I didn't have to spend a lot of time searching. The application tracker was helpful too because it kept everything organized in one place, making the whole job search feel a lot less stressful.
assessment.preserve: The AI CV analysis should remain unchanged because it's one of the platform's strongest features. It provides quick and useful feedback that helps users improve their resumes. I also think the clean, simple interface should stay the same, as it's easy to navigate and makes the overall experience smooth.
assessment.priority_improvement: The first improvement should be making the job recommendations more accurate and personalized. Matching jobs more closely to a user's skills, experience, location, and career interests would make the platform much more useful and save users time.
assessment.priority_reason: I would prioritize improving the job matching feature first, since it's one of the main reasons people use the platform. After that, I'd focus on making the CV feedback more personalized. Next, I'd enhance the application tracker by adding reminders and notes, and finally, improve the overall user experience with better navigation and onboarding.
assessment.product_understanding: Myro is like a personal career assistant that helps people find jobs and improve their chances of getting hired. You can upload your resume, and it gives AI-powered feedback on what you can improve, like formatting, keywords, and overall quality. It also recommends jobs that match your profile, lets you save interesting opportunities, and helps you keep track of all your applications in one place. Overall, it makes the job search process much easier, more organized, and increases your chances of getting noticed by recruiters.
assessment.reproduction_steps: Myro helps us understand how strong our resume is, which jobs match our skills, and where we can improve to increase our chances of getting hired. It also gives a clear view of our application progress, making it easier to stay organized and know what to do next.
assessment.return_trigger: I would return to Myro whenever we're updating our resume, looking for new job opportunities, or tracking our job applications.
